objective: Separate classification uncertainty/OOD semantics from scientific-anomaly evidence in the production result and API contracts.

baseline.description: Production results exposed OOD diagnostics, while Workbench/API semantics could present anomaly terminology without an explicit scientific-anomaly contract.

expected_improvement: Make scientific anomaly an explicit, independent result channel.
Prevent OOD diagnostics from being interpreted as astrophysical anomaly evidence.
Keep the current v0.2 production model fail-safe: no scientific-anomaly detector is claimed.

evidence: ScientificAnomalyResult contract validates status, alignment, finiteness and explicit method/version.
PredictionResult and API schemas preserve separate OOD and scientific_anomaly fields.
Regression tests cover available, not_evaluated and invalid mixed states.
Workbench diagnostic view now renders the channels independently.

findings: OOD anomaly_score terminology is an implementation diagnostic and does not establish astrophysical anomaly.
The prior UI grouped OOD and anomaly diagnostics under a combined label, creating semantic ambiguity.
OOD, classification uncertainty, and scientific anomaly require independent contract fields and statuses.
The current v0.2 production model must keep scientific_anomaly_status=not_evaluated unless a dedicated analysis mode supplies evidence.

knowledge_carried_forward: Scientific anomaly remains a future explicit analysis mode rather than a reinterpretation of the existing OOD model.
Scientific Validation remains release-blocking and is not weakened by this architectural change.
